title: MRMhub
text:
MRMhub is an open-source toolchain for targeted Multiple Reaction Monitoring (MRM) mass spectrometry — the assay type used for quantitative lipidomics and metabolomics. It takes data from raw instrument files to quality-controlled, quantitative results: peak integration, QC, normalisation, drift and batch correction, calibration, and reporting.
It is intended for analytical scientists and biochemists who run targeted assays — the tutorials require running R scripts rather than writing them — as well as for bioinformaticians who build reproducible pipelines. MRMhub consists of two modules that can be used independently:

title: MRMhub
text:
Why MRMhub?

Reproducible. Every step is code — parameter files for INTEGRATOR, R scripts for QUANT.
Modular. Each module replaces or augments existing pipeline components without lock-in.
MRM-specific. Drift correction, batch correction (Broadhurst 2018), ISTD/calibration quantitation, isotope-interference correction, and the QC vocabulary (BQC, TQC, SBLK, …) built into one container object. The terminology is defined in the Key Concepts & Glossary ↗.
